question: Should OpenClaw accept the experimental Claws lifecycle in core and retain `CLAW.md` as its canonical exported manifest format, rather than keeping Claw package distribution and authoring outside the core roadmap?
rationale: This PR is technically bounded but changes the public package-authoring and export contract of an unshipped, multi-PR experimental subsystem; only maintainers can decide whether that subsystem and its canonical format belong in core.

options.title: Sponsor the stacked Claws lifecycle
options.body: Accept the parent lifecycle direction, require exact-head end-to-end proof, then review this final format layer as part of the complete stack.

options.title: Defer the core feature
options.body: Keep the PR unmerged until maintainers choose a narrower core boundary or an external package-distribution path.

options.title: Reject the core direction
options.body: Close the associated stack with a documented alternative if core Claw package lifecycle support is not planned.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the stacked Claws lifecycle
recommendation.body: Accept the parent lifecycle direction, require exact-head end-to-end proof, then review this final format layer as part of the complete stack.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the demonstrated owner of the active Claws series and can supply the requested lifecycle evidence while maintainer reviewers make the product decision.
